content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: outage message, chat deflection, callback and a 3-agent move to payments, no break delays. Predicted 89.9% service level for ₹816.","why":"The jump in payments calls is driven by the UPI switch P1 incident (INC-20261006-6998), not by staffing or handle time. At 10:30, 213 calls arrived against 111.9 forecast, service level dropped to 4.7% and 59 calls were abandoned. Over the last four intervals, upi_payment_failed calls ran at 2.56x normal. R1 addresses that demand directly. It plays an IVR outage message for UPI-related reasons from 12:30 to 14:30, deflects 20% of status and refund enquiries to chat, offers callback from 12:30 to 14:00, and moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments from 12:15 to 14:00. It is predicted to reach 89.9% overall (payments 88.1%, general 92.4%) with 2.2% abandon. That clears the 80% target, at ₹816, with no policy violations. Doing nothing is forecast to leave us at 77.9%, with payments at 70.9%, below target.","trade_offs":["P1 costs nothing and reaches 86.7%, but it delays payments breaks and breaches BRK-04 (12 agents would have more than one break delayed today).","P2 matches R1's cost (₹816) and overall 89.9%, with payments slightly higher at 89.5%. It also breaches BRK-04 because of the break delays.","R2 is the policy-safe step up: 94.1% and 1.1% abandon, but at ₹5,766 for overtime to 20 payments agents. That is about 7x the cost for roughly 4 extra points when the target is already met.","Risk to general is low. Even after losing 3 agents, general is predicted at 92.4%, higher than the 88.3% it would see with no action."],"watch":"Check payments service level at 12:45 and 13:15 against the 88.1% prediction, and track chat and callback uptake. If the UPI incident is not resolved by 14:30, or payments drops toward 80%, consider moving to R2 (overtime) rather than delaying breaks."}
